Heard Mr. G. Taloh, learned counsel for the petitioner. Also heard Mr. T.
Ete, learned Public Prosecutor for the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
This is an application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973, for grant of bail to the accused, who has been languishing in
Page No.# 2/4
jail hazot in connection with Rupa P.S. Case No. 21/2022, under Sections
120(B)/170/186/353/364(A)/ 34 of the Indian Penal Code read with Sections
15(c)/16(b)/18 of UAP Act.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. G. Taloh, that
the accused was arrested in connection with the present case on 06.12.2022
and since then he is behind the bar. Further it is submitted that the another co-
accused, Shri Micheal Tajo, has already been granted bail by this Court
yesterday, i.e. on 21.02.2023, in BA No. 12/2023, and accordingly prayed to
consider the bail prayer for the present accused on the ground of parity. Further
it is submitted that the present accused is an employee under the prime
accused- Shri Micheal Tajo and he was not at all involved in any offence as
alleged in the F.I.R. Further it is submitted that on 16.01.2023, a petition for bail
was moved before the learned Sessions Judge, Bomdila, but the same was
rejected and hence the present petition has been filed seeking bail for the
present accused. It is also submitted that the victim has already arrived at an
amicable settlement with the prime accused- Shri Micheal Tajo and a copy of the
said Deed of Agreement is also annexed as Annexure-3 to the petition. Further
it is submitted that the present accused is a permanent resident of his
addressed locality and hence there is no chance of absconding if the accused is
enlarged on bail. More so, he will regularly appear before the learned Court
below and will co-operate in the trial of the case. The accused is behind the bar
since 06.12.2022 and considering his length of detention also, the accused be
released on bail.
In this context, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Mr. T. Ete, also
Page No.# 3/4
submitted that the co-accused has already been released on bail yesterday, i.e.
on 21.02.2023, in BA No. 12/2023, considering the amicable settlement arrived
at between the parties and hence, considering the length of detention and on
the ground of parity, the bail petition for the present accused can also be
considered.
After hearing the submissions of learned counsels of both sides, I have
perused the LCR, which is available before this Court as it was called for in
connection with BA/12/2023.
It is an admitted fact that the accused is behind the bar for last more than
80 days and hence, I find that further custodial detention of the present
accused is not necessary and in the same time, also considering the amicable
settlement arrived at between the prime accused and the victim as well as other
aspects of the case, I find that further custodial interrogation of the accused
seems to be not necessary here in this case.
Accordingly, it is provided that on furnishing a bond of Rs. 20,000/-
(Rupees twenty thousand) only with one surety of like amount to the
satisfaction of the learned Sessions Judge, Bomdila, the accused, namely, Shri
Samsul Ali, be enlarged on bail, subject to the following conditions:
(i) that the accused shall make himself available for interrogation by
the Investigating Officer as and when required;
Page No.# 4/4
(ii) that the accused shall not, directly or indirectly, make any
inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the
facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to
the Court or to any police officer; and
(iii) that the accused shall not leave the jurisdiction of the learned
Sessions Judge, Bomdila, without prior permission.
In terms of above, this bail application stands disposed of.

Heard Mr. C. Modi, learned counsel for the petitioner. Also heard Ms. T.
Jini, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State of Arunachal Pradesh and
Mr. J. Riram, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant and also
assisted the learned Additional Public Prosecutor.
Page No.# 2/5
This is an application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973, praying for grant of pre-arrest bail to the accused/petitioner,
who is apprehending arrest in connection with Nirjuli P.S. Case No. 08/2023,
under Sections 341/326/506 of the Indian Penal Code, corresponding to G.R.
No. 91/2023.
The Case Diary has been received and I have perused the same.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. C. Modi, that
the accused/petitioner is innocent and no way involved in the alleged offence.
Both the informant and the accused were good friends and they were staying in
the same building and the accused/petitioner was the tenant of the victim. It is
a fact that the incident had happened while they both went to a Bar and after
some time, the accused/petitioner proposed to leave the Bar, but the victim was
keep on insisting him to take alcohol till next morning around 3:30 a.m. The
owner/Bar Manager has annoyed them and was trying to drive them out the Bar
and in order to scare the Manager of the Bar, the present accused/petitioner
took out his dao and in the meantime, the victim was trying to stop the
accused/petitioner and was trying to snatch the dao from the
accused/petitioner, the victim, suddenly, got hurt and sustained cut injury from
the dao of the accused/petitioner. He had no intention to cause hurt to the
victim and the incident was happened only to scare the Manager of the Bar and
the accused/petitioner, being a friend of the victim, took the victim to the
hospital for treatment also. The accused/petitioner is willing and ready to co-
operate with the I.O. in the further investigation of this case if he is granted
Page No.# 3/5
with the privilege of pre-arrest bail. Further, the accused/petitioner is the sole
earning member of the entire family and in the event of his arrest, his entire
family will suffer. Accordingly, the learned counsel for the petitioner prayed for
granting the accused/petitioner with the privilege of pre-arrest bail.
In this context, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Ms. T. Jini, has
submitted that the I.O. has recorded the statements of the witnesses and the
medical report is also collected by the I.O. and as per the medical report, the
injury sustained by the informant/victim is of simple in nature caused by sharp
object. Further it is submitted that as per the note of the I.O., it reveals that
they have collected the CCTV footage and the statement of the witnesses are
also been recorded. However, the weapon, which was used in the commission of
the offence, has not yet been recovered.
The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant/victim, Mr. J.
Riram, has submitted that it is a fact that both the victim and the
accused/petitioner were friends and the accused/petitioner is a tenant under
him and it is also a fact that on the day of incident, the victim along with one of
his friend went to the Bar, where the accused/petitioner was already there, and
they had alcohol at that time. But, suddenly after some altercation, the
accused/petitioner took a long sharp dao and tried to assault the Manager of
the Bar and when the present informant/victim tried to stop him and in that
process, the accused inflicted injury on his person and he sustained grievous
injuries on his head as well as near the abdomen. Further it is submitted by the
learned counsel for the informant/victim that if the accused/petitioner is granted
Page No.# 4/5
with the privilege of pre-arrest bail, in that event, there is every possibility of
threatening or hampering the investigation of the case. Accordingly, it is prayed
that the accused/petitioner should not be granted with the privilege of pre-
arrest bail.
After hearing the submissions of learned counsels of both sides and also
on perusal of the Case Diary, it appears that the case was registered under
Section 326 of the Indian Penal Code and it seems that the victim himself
lodged the F.I.R. after 6-7 hours later of the incident, which otherwise reveals
that he was not admitted in the hospital for the injuries sustained by him. In the
same time, considering the progress of the investigation and also considering
the medical documents and injuries sustained by the victim/informant, I find
that custodial interrogation of the present accused/petitioner is not necessary in
this case therefore, I find it a fit case to extend the privilege of pre-arrest bail to
the accused/petitioner.
Accordingly, it is provided that in the event of arrest of the
accused/petitioner, namely, Shri Biri Kama, in connection with Nirjuli P.S. Case
No. 08/2023, under Sections 341/326/506 of the Indian Penal Code,
corresponding to G.R. No. 91/2023, he shall be enlarged on pre-arrest bail on
his executing a bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees twenty thousand) only with one
surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting authority, subject to the
following conditions:
(i) that the petitioner shall appear before the Investigating
Officer of the case within a period of 1 (one) week from
today;
Page No.# 5/5
(ii) that the petitioner shall fully co-operate with the
investigation of the case and shall appear before the
Investigating Officer as and when required in connection
with the investigation of the aforesaid P.S. Case; and
(iii) that the petitioner shall not, directly or indirectly, make
any inducement, threat or promise to any person
acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade
him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any
police officer.
The anticipatory bail application stands disposed of in terms above.
The Case Diary be sent back.

Heard Mr. L. Tatam, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. G. Tado,
learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
Page No.# 2/4
2. This joint application, under Section 482 of the Cr.P.C., has been filed by
2(two) petitioners, namely; 1. Shri Sunit Sagar and 2. Shri Likha Tara, for
quashing the F.I.R. of Naharlagun P.S. Case No. 138/2019, under Section 381
IPC, on the ground that the said case has already been settled between the
parties amicably.
3. It is to be noted here that Naharlagun P. S. Case No. 138/2019 under
Section 381 IPC has been registered on the basis of one F.I.R. lodged by the
petitioner no. 2, Shri Likha Tara on 15.08.2019.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that after registration of
the case, investigation was carried out and the same culminated in
submission of Charge-sheet against the present petitioner under Section 381
IPC and now the case is pending before the Court of leaner Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Yupia. The learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that
the matter has already been compounded between the 2 (two) petitioners
and to that effect a Deed of Settlement was also executed on 22.11.2023,
which has been enclosed to the petition as Annexure no. 4, and as the
matter has already been settled between the parties, the learned counsel for
the petitioner submits that the matter may be disposed of by quashing and
setting aside the F.I.R. and the Charge-sheet, pending before the Court of
the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Yupia.
5. Mr. G. Tado, learned Additional Public Prosecutor on the other hand
submits that here the petitioner no. 1 has been charge-sheeted under
Section 381 IPC and the same is compoundable with permission of the Court
as per Section 320 of the Cr.P.C, and as the matter stands compounded
between the parties, the state has no objection in the event of allowing the
Page No.# 3/4
petition.
6. Having heard the submissions of the learned Advocates of both sides, I
have gone through the petition and the documents placed on record and
also perused the Deed of Settlement dated 22.11.2023 (annexed as
Annexure-4).
7. It appears from the record that the case has been registered under
Section 381 IPC on the basis of F.I.R. lodged by the petitioner no.2, namely,
Shri Likha Tara. The essence of allegation made in the F.I.R. dated
rd
15.08.2019, is that on 23 July, 2019, Hero Honda Karizma bike, belonging
to his son, was stolen by his driver from Naharlagun. It also appears from
the record that after completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer
had submitted Charge-sheet against the petitioner no. 1 to stand trial under
Section 381 IPC.
8. It also appears that the Offence under Section 381 IPC is compoundable
with permission of the Court as per Section 320 Cr.P.C. The Deed of
Settlement, dated 22.11.2023, indicates that both the petitioners have
mutually compounded the matter and that they shall also maintain peace
and harmony and shall not recall the bygone incident.
9. In view of above, this Court is of the considered opinion that this is a fit
case where the F.I.R. and the Charge-sheet can be quashed by invoking the
provision of Section 482 Cr.P.C. as the same will advance the cause of
justice, and as the matter stands compounded, the petitioner No.2 is unlikely
to depose against the petitioner No.1 in the court during the trial. And on
such court allowing the proceeding to continue in the learned court below
Page No.# 4/4
will be an abuse of the process of the court.
10. Accordingly, the F.I.R. of Naharlagun P.S. Case No. 138/2019, under
Section 381 IPC stands quashed and set aside.
11. In terms of above, this Criminal Petition stands disposed of.
JUDGE
Comparing Assistant

ORDER
Date : 18-04-2023
Heard Ms. T. Y. Bhutia, learned counsel for the petitioner. Also heard Mr. J.
Tsering, learned Public Prosecutor for the State respondent No. 1 and 2.
This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973, praying for quashing and setting aside of Order dated
13.02.2023, passed by the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner-cum-
Executive Magistrate, Kalaktang, West Kameng District, whereby, the petitioner
along with other parties concerned were directed to maintain status quo and
refrain from carrying out any sort of activity in the disputed area.
Ms. T. Y. Bhutia, learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the
disputed land belongs to the present petitioner and the said land was gifted to
her by her father on 23.10.2012. Thereafter, the complainants namely, Shri
Urjen Kharma, Shri Rinchin Kharma and Shri Sonam Phuntso filed a complaint
letter against the present petitioner along with other concerned parties before
the Additional Commissioner, West Kameng District on the ground of tress-
passing their private land by way of distraction of fencing, cutting trees and
digging by knowing the fact that the case is pending before the Gaoh Burah,
Chingi village for passing the judgment.
It is further submitted that from the order passed by the learned
Additional Deputy Commissioner-cum-Executive Magistrate, Kalaktang, it reveals
Page No.# 3/4
that the Executive Magistrate had passed the order to maintain status quo until
the settlement of the case. However, as per the Arunachal Pradesh Civil Courts
Act, 2021, the Deputy Commissioner or the Assistant Commissioner, no longer
has the power to adjudicate either civil or criminal matters within the State of
Arunachal Pradesh and have fallen out of the purview of a Civil Court under the
Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945, and that any
proceedings under Section 145/146 of the Cr.P.C cannot proceed once the Civil
Court is seized of the matter as the possession is eventually to be determined
by the Civil Court, which in this case, is the village authority. Hence, this petition
u/s 482 of the Cr.P.C. for setting aside and to quash the impugned order dated
13.02.2023.
Further, the learned counsel for the petitioner also relied on the decision
passed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in Crl.No.5444/2022 dated 01.11.2022,
wherein, it has been held that “once the Civil Court is seized of the matter, it
goes without saying that the proceedings under Section 145/146 Cr.P.C. cannot
proceed and must come to an end”.
In this regard, Mr. J. Tsering, the learned Public Prosecutor submitted that
the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner-cum-Executive Magistrate,
Kalaktang, had passed the impugned order without following the mandate
required as per section 145 of the Cr.P.C. by directing the parties to maintain
peace and tranquility of the said disputed land.
He also relied on the decision of the Hon’ble Apex Court reported in 1984
(0) Supreme (SC) 361, wherein, it has been held that;
Page No.# 4/4
“……..when a civil litigation is pending for the property wherein the
question of possession is involved and has been adjudicated, we see hardly any
justification for initiating parallel criminal proceedings under Section 145 of the
code.”
Considering the submissions made by the learned Advocates of both sides
and also considering the entire facts of the case, it is seen that the learned
Additional Deputy Commissioner-cum-Executive Magistrate, Kalaktang had
passed the order under Section 145 Cr.P.C. despite knowing the fact that the
matter is pending before the Civil Forum.
So considering the entire aspect of the case and also considering the view
of the Hon’ble Supreme Court, the impugned order dated 13.02.2023, passed
by the learned Additional Deputy Commissioner-cum-Executive Magistrate,
Kalaktang, stand set aside and quashed.
In terms of above, this criminal petition stands disposed of.
JUDGE

had no intention to grow poppy in their cultivated field and it was the poppy
plants that were grown up their own because they mixed the poppy seeds along
with the mustard seeds. The accused/petitioner being lady, her entire family and
children are facing problems in her absence. Moreover, she will corporate with
the I.O for further investigation of this case and will also appear before the I.O
as and when required. She is in custody since last one month and hence,
considering her length of detention, she may be allowed to go on bail.

that the statements of all the accused persons were recorded by the I.O and
from the statement made by the accused persons, it reveals that they saw the
mixing mustards seeds along with the poppy seeds, for which unfortunately,
while they were cultivating, some poppy plants grown up. But coming to know

poppy plants. However, it is submitted by the learned Additional Public

respondent No. 2 entered into a mutual settlement agreement on 14.07.2023
and accordingly, considering the mutual agreement between the parties, viz-a-
viz the other aspects of the case, the present petition may be allowed by
invoking the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 of the Code of
Criminal Procedure by setting aside and quashing the criminal proceeding in
G.R. Case No. 46/2009, corresponding to Tezu P.S. Case No. 46/2009, under
Sections 341/149/323 of the Indian Penal Code, pending before the Court of
learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Tezu.
4. In this context, Ms. T. Jini, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, submits
that as the matter has already been compromised between the parties, the
State has no objection in the event the petition is allowed by quashing the said
criminal proceeding. However, she submitted that the present petition is filed
only on behalf of Shri Cholingso Kora and hence, the petition may be allowed for
quashing the criminal proceeding in G.R. Case No. 46/2009 only in respect of
the present petitioner.
5. Mr. T. Taggu, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the respondent No. 2,
also submitted that the matter has already been settled between the parties and
one deed of settlement is also executed on 14.07.2023 and hence, he has no
objection if the present petition is allowed.
6. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsels appearing for
Page No.# 4/4
the parties and the nature of offence, viz-a-viz the settlement agreement arrived
at between the parties, I find that this is a fit case to exercise the power under
Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the criminal
proceeding in G.R. Case No. 46/2009 only against the present petitioner.
7. Accordingly, the petition is allowed. The criminal proceeding in G.R. Case
No. 46/2009, corresponding to Tezu P.S. Case No. 46/2009, under Sections
341/149/323 of the Indian Penal Code, pending before the Court of learned
Chief Judicial Magistrate, Tezu, in respect of the present petitioner, is hereby set
aside and quashed.
8. However, the learned Court below shall proceed with the case in respect of
the other co-accused.
9. In terms of above, this criminal petition stands disposed of.
JUDGE
Comparing Assistant

judgments.text:
Page No.# 1/6
GAHC040006802023
THE GAUHATI HIGH COURT
(HIGH COURT OF ASSAM, NAGALAND, MIZORAM AND ARUNACHAL PRADESH)
(ITANAGAR BENCH)
Case No. : Crl.Petn. 90/2023
1:Aman Mangam and Anr.
S/o Shri Hopi Mangam,
Present Add. Boso Colony, Seppa, PO/PS Seppa, East Kameng District, Arunachal
Pradesh,
Permanent Add. Vill Mangfi Mangam, PO Sawa, PS Chayang Tajo, District East
Kameng, (AP)
Mobile No. 8257863664
2: Minu Nabam Mangam
W/o Shri Aman Mangam
Present Add. Boso Colony
Seppa
PO/PS Seppa
East Kameng District
Arunachal Pradesh.
Mobile No. 961265068
VERSUS
1:THE STATE OF AP
Represented through Public Prosecutor.
Advocate for the Petitioner : R Taku
Advocate for the Respondent : P P of AP
Page No.# 2/6
BEFORE
HONBLE MR. JUSTICE KARDAK ETE
ORDER
Date : 09-06-2023
Heard Ms. Lipi Niri, learned counsel for the petitioners and Ms. T. Jini,
learned Additional PP for the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
2. This application under Section 482 of CrPC, 1973 has been jointly filed
by the petitioners praying for quashing of the charge sheet No. 121/2018 arising
out of Itanagar Women PS case No. 104/2018 under Section 376(1)/417 of IPC,
1860 and proceeding of Sessions case No. 26/2019 (YPA) pending before the
District & Session Judge, Yupia, Arunachal Pradesh on the basis of settlement
entered into between the petitioners.
3. The petitioners are husband and wife and they were living together
since 2016, however, when the petitioner No. 2 suspected the petitioner No. 1
of having illicit relationship with some other woman, out of anger and
misunderstanding, she filed the FIR against the petitioner No. 1 at Itanagar
Women PS on 22.11.2018 under the misguidance of some other person. The
FIR was registered as Itanagar Women PS Case no. 104/ 2018 under Section
376(1)/417 of IPC, 1860. On completion of investigation, charge sheet no.
121/2018 was filed against the petitioner No. 1 which is pending at the stage of
appearance being Session case No. 26/2019(YPA) before the Session Judge,
Yupia.
4. After few months of reconciliation made by the relatives of both sides,
the petitioners have entered into a Kebang/NYELE in the year 2019 and they
Page No.# 3/6
have compromised and settled the matter. Moreover, they are blessed with two
children and both of them are living a happy married life.
5. Ms. Lipi Niri, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the FIR
was filed by the petitioner No. 2 against the petitioner No. 1 out of anger and
misunderstanding as she has suspected her husband of having an illicit
relationship with some other woman. After coming to the actual facts, the
parties have entered into a settlement and are living as husband and wife with
two children. Since the parties have entered into a settlement between them
and they are living peacefully and happily, the Session case No. 26/2019(YPA)
may be quashed in the interest of justice.
6. Ms. T. Jini, learned Additional PP fairly submits that though the offence
is under Section 376 of IPC, 1860, on perusal of the statements of the parties
and the materials available on record, it does not support the case of the
prosecution as the FIR has been filed when there was misunderstanding
between the petitioners, and thereafter, they started living as husband and wife
peacefully and happily. She further submits that the based on the materials
available on record the possibility of chance of conviction is remote and bleak
and therefore, the present case is fit to be allowed by quashing the session case
being Session case No. 26/2019(YPA)
7. I have considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the
parties and also gone through the materials available on record. On perusal of
the statement of the petitioner No. 2 as well as other witnesses recorded under
section 164 and 161 of Cr.PC, it discloses no ingredients of section 376 IPC,
rather at best it is a case of infidelity against the petitioner No. 1 in as much as
Page No.# 4/6
the allegation made by the petitioner No. 2 is that, while having a relationship
with her the petitioner No. 1 was also having a relationship with some other
woman and made false promise of marriage. By now, the parties are living
happily with their two children and settlement deed has been entered into
without there being any coercion or threat from any corner.
8. This Court may profitably refer to the law enunciated by the Hon’ble
Supreme Court in the case of the State of Madhya Pradesh Vs. Lakshmi
Narayan and Ors., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 which is reproduced herein
below:
“15. Considering the law on the point and the other decisions of this Court on the
point, referred to hereinabove, it is observed and held as under:
i) that the power conferred under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal
proceedings for the non-compoundable offences under Section 320 of the Code can be
exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character, particularly
those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship
or family disputes and when the parties have resolved the entire dispute amongst
themselves;
ii) such power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involved heinous
and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc.
Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society;
iii) similarly, such power is not to be exercised for the offences under the special
statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants
while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of
compromise between the victim and the offender;
iv) offences under Section 307 IPC and the Arms Act etc. would fall in the
category of heinous and serious offences and therefore are to be treated as crime
against the society and not against the individual alone, and therefore, the criminal
proceedings for the offence under Section 307 IPC and/or the Arms Act etc. which have
a serious impact on the society cannot be quashed in exercise of powers under Section
482 of the Code, on the ground that the parties have resolved their entire dispute
amongst themselves. However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely
because there is a mention of Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under
this provision. It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether
incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has
collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under
Section 307 IPC. For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the
Page No.# 5/6
nature of injury sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of
the body, nature of weapons used etc. However, such an exercise by the High Court
would be permissible only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the
charge sheet is filed/charge is framed and/or during the trial. Such exercise is not
permissible when the matter is still under investigation. Therefore, the ultimate
conclusion in paragraphs 29.6 and 29.7 of the decision of this Court in the case of
Narinder Singh (supra) should be read harmoniously and to be read as a whole and in
the circumstances stated hereinabove;
v) while exercising the power under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal
proceedings in respect of non-compoundable offences, which are private in nature and
do not have a serious impart on society, on the ground that there is a
settlement/compromise between the victim and the offender, the High Court is required
to consider the antecedents of the accused; the conduct of the accused, namely,
whether the accused was absconding and why he was absconding, how he had
managed with the complainant to enter into a compromise etc. “
9. In the case of Kapil Gupta V. State of NCT of Delhi, (2022) SCC
Online SC 1030, the Hon’ble Supreme Court held that the Court while exercising
its power under section 482 Cr.PC, the Court should be slow in quashing the
proceedings wherein heinous and serious offences are involved, but is not
foreclosed from examining as to whether there exists material for incorporation
of such an offence or as to whether there is sufficient evidence which if proved
would lead to proving the charge for the offence charged with. The Court has
also to take into consideration as to whether the settlement between the parties
is going to result into harmony between them which may improve their mutual
relationship
.
10. On the careful consideration of the case at hand as noted above,
both the petitioners are living peacefully and happily as husband and wife with
their two children. They have entered into a settlement on their own volition to
maintain peace and harmony between them and the society at large. The
materials placed before this Court discloses no ingredients of offences under
Section 376 and the chance of conviction is quite remote and bleak.
Page No.# 6/6
11. In view of the above, this Court is of the considered view that this is
a fit case where the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 482 Cr.PC,
1973 deserves to be exercised.
12. Accordingly, the charge sheet No. 121/2018 arising out of Itanagar
Women PS case No. 104/2018 under Section 376(1)/417 of IPC, 1860 and
proceeding of Sessions case No. 26/2019 (YPA) pending before the District &
Session Judge, Yupia, Arunachal Pradesh is hereby set aside and quashed.
13. In the result, the criminal petition is allowed and disposed of.
JUDGE
Comparing Assistant

judgments.case_name: AB/143/2022 of Goka Tao Vs THE STATE OF AP
judgments.text:
Page No.# 1/8
GAHC040015492022
THE GAUHATI HIGH COURT
(HIGH COURT OF ASSAM, NAGALAND, MIZORAM AND ARUNACHAL PRADESH)
(ITANAGAR BENCH)
Case No. : AB 143/2022
1:Goka Tao
Son of Margo Tao, a permanent resident of village-Siji, P.O and P.S-Likhabali,
District- Lower Siang, Arunachal Pradesh.
VERSUS
1:THE STATE OF AP
Represented through Public Prosecutor
Advocate for the Petitioner : T T Tara
Advocate for the Respondent : P P of AP
BEFORE
HONBLE MR. JUSTICE NANI TAGIA
ORDER
Date : 22-05-2023
Heard Mr. T. T. Tara, learned counsel for the applicant. Also heard Ms. L.
Hage, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State of Arunachal
Pradesh and Mr. L. Perme, learned counsel for the complainant.
2. This is an application, filed under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C., praying for
grant of pre-arrest bail to the applicant in connection with Aalo P.S. Case No.
49/2022, registered under Sections 468/471/34 IPC, 1860.
Page No.# 2/8
3. The aforesaid Aalo P.S. Case No. 49/2022, under Sections 468/471/34
IPC, 1860, was registered on an F.I.R. dated 14.09.2022, lodged by one Shri
Iken Tao, before the Officer-in-charge, Police Station Aalo, against as may as
5 (five) persons including the applicant, alleging commission of criminal
conspiracy, impersonation, forgery to cause financial losses/damages and
wrongful use of lawful authority/courts(s).
4. The applicant, along with 4 (four) other alleged accused had filed an
anticipatory bail application being AB No. 3015/2022, at principal seat of this
Court at Guwahati, for grant of pre-arrest bail to the applicants, therein. The
aforesaid AB No. 3015/2022 was considered by the Court and vide order
dated 13.12.2022, the anticipatory bail application filed by the applicants,
therein, which included the applicant herein, was rejected.
5. The order dated 13.12.2022, passed in AB No. 3015/2022 is reproduced
hereinbelow:
Date : 13-12-2022
Heard Mr. A. K. Bhattacharyya, learned senior Advocate assisted by Mr. D.
K. Bhattacharyya, learned counsel and Mr. G. Alam, learned counsel appearing
on behalf of the applicants. Also heard Mr. NNB Choudhury, learned Additional
A.G.-cum-Public Prosecutor for the State of Arunachal Pradesh assisted by Mr.
A. Chandran, learned Additional Senior Government Advocate representing the
State of Arunachal Pradesh as well as Mr. L. Perme, learned counsel appearing
on behalf of the informant.
2. This application is filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,
1973, praying for seeking Anticipatory Bail to the applicants in connection
with Aalo P.S. Case No.49/2022, under Sections 468/471/34 of the IPC, 1860,
and corresponding G.R. Case No.103/2022.
3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the applicants that;
(i) The applicant No.1 is one of the partners of M/s Frontier Stone Crusher Unit
having its administrative office at Dona Planet, G.S. Road, Guwahati. The
applicant No. 1 is also a Director of Khasi Ispat Pvt. Ltd. with its registered
Page No.# 3/8
office at S.J. Road, Athgaon, Guwahati.
(ii) The applicant No. 2 is a businessman dealing with supply of stone
materials.
(iii) The applicant No.3 is an employee of M/s Frontier Stone Crusher Unit and
is engaged as a Supervisor in its Stone Crusher Unit at Siji Village, Likabali.
(iv) The applicant No.4 is the landowner of a plot of land where the Stone
Crusher of M/s Frontier Stone Crusher Unit is located.
(v) The applicant No.5 is practicing as an Advocate in Aalo, Arunachal Pradesh.
(vi) And the informant Shri Iken Tao is also a partner of M/s Frontier Stone
Crusher Unit, who had informed the Officer-in-Charge, Aalo Police Station, inter
alia, that he had entered into a partnership with the applicant No.1 and the
partnership deed was executed before the Executive Magistrate, Likabali on
27.11.2020, by fraudulently incorporating the words “or for 30 years from date
of commencement of agreement” in Clause 2.1 of the said partnership deed,
and the same was presented for registration before the Sub-Registrar(S&R),
West Siang, Aalo, Arunachal Pradesh. It was further alleged that the applicant
No.4 had impersonated him and submitting his Land Possession Certificate
(LPC) as supporting documents had aided in the fraudulent registration of the
said partnership deed.
4. Further, it is stated that the applicant No.5, who is a practicing Advocate and
well known to the informant since childhood, had aided in registration of the
said partnership deed. On the basis of the said information, Aalo P.S. Case
No.49/2022, under Sections 468/471/34 of the IPC was registered and
assigned G.R. Case No.103/2022. It is further submitted that the applicants
categorically denied their involvement in the offence alleged and are sought to
be unnecessarily harassed in connection with Aalo P.S. Case No.49/2022. The
informant, being the proprietor of M/s Frontier Stone Crusher Unit had license
for operating the Stone Crusher at Siji Village, Likabali and he was also
desirous to enter into a partnership deed with the applicant No.1 and Khasi
Ispat Pvt. Ltd. Accordingly, on 27.11.2020, a Deed of Partnership was executed
before the Executive Magistrate, Likabali, Arunachal Pradesh and was
presented for registration before the Sub-Registrar(S&R), Aalo, West Siang
District, Arunachal Pradesh and assigned registration No.LD-15/21 dated
13.05.2021. After registration of the partnership deed a copies of the
agreement was given to the applicants as well as to the informant, and hence,
the informant is well aware of the contents of the said registered partnership
deed. The informant was also provided a Hydraulic Excavator and 3(three)
Tata Signa 2823 Dumpers for smooth supply of materials to the Stone Crusher.
But the informant could not supply the requisite quantity of materials to the
Page No.# 4/8
Stone Crusher and also did not allow procuring of the materials from the third
parties as well as blocked the approach road. Apart from that on 14.07.2021,
the informant assaulted the staff of the Stone Crusher and threatened them
with dire consequences and also destroyed assets of Stone Crusher. In the
meantime the informant stopped supplying materials to the Stone Crusher and
served a letter dated 22.06.2021, stating that the partnership business could
continue only on revision of the rates of the supplied materials, otherwise he
would withdraw his license from the partnership business. Thereafter, the
applicant No.1 requested the informant to hand over the Excavator and three
Dumpers but the informant refused to hand over the same and for which the
applicant No.1 and Khasi Ispat Pvt. Ltd., had jointly filed the application under
Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in the Court of the
learned Additional District Judge No.2, Kamrup(M), Guwahati for granting
appropriate interim order. Accordingly, the learned Court passed the order
dated 25.03.2022, directing the instant informant to hand over the excavator
and three dumpers to the applicant No.1. But the informant did not hand over
the said materials and disobeyed the order passed by the learned Additional
District Judge No.2, Kamrup(M), Guwahati dated 25.03.2022.
5. The learned counsel for the applicants also submits that after registration of
the partnership deed, a copy of the same was supplied to the informant and
hence, he was fully aware of the words “or for 30 years from date of
commencement of agreement” of Clause 2.1 of the partnership deed. Thus, the
applicants states that when there is specific clause of rescinding the
partnership business on mutual agreement, there is no point of fraudulently
incorporating the words “or for 30 years from date of commencement of
agreement” which are redundant, if the parties do not desire to continue the
partnership business. Further, it is stated that there is no functional Treasury
Office at Likabali in Lower Siang District for registration of documents and for
which the partnership deed had to be registered before the Sub-Registrar
(S&R), Aalo, Arunachal Pradesh after its execution on 27.11.2020 before the
Executive Magistrate, Likabali. The applicant No.4 is no way connected with
the business of M/s Frontier Stone Crusher Unit and he is only the landowner of
a plot of land, where the Stone Crusher is located. Similarly, the applicant No.5
is practicing Advocate in Aalo, Arunachal Pradesh and hence, no way connected
with the business of M/s Frontier Stone Crusher Unit and he merely rendered
his professional services as an Advocate for registration of the partnership
deed.
6. Further, it is also stated that the dispute was between the informant and the
applicant No.1 and it is purely civil in nature but, the informant by alleging
fraudulent incorporation of some words, has tried to give a colour of criminal
offence against the present applicants. The police are in search of the
applicants in connection with Aalo P.S. Case No.49/2022, and hence, due to
Page No.# 5/8
reasonable apprehension of being arrested on accusation of committing a non-
bailable offence. Therefore, the applicants approached this Court with the
present application seeking Anticipatory Bail. All the applicants are from
respected families and have no criminal records and there are no chances of
absconding or hampering or tempering of the evidences during the
investigation of the case. Rather, they will extend their full corporation in the
investigation of this case, if they are granted with the privilege of pre-arrest
bail.
7. Mr. Choudhury, learned Additional A.G.-cum-Public Prosecutor for the State
of Arunachal Pradesh submits that it reveals from the Case Diary that the
applicants forged the documents i.e. the partnership deed by inserting the line
“or for 30 years from date of commencement of agreement”, which was
fraudulently incorporated and has changed the nature and character of the
agreement. He also submits that custodial interrogations of all the applicants
are necessary and hence, it is not a fit case to extend the privilege of pre-arrest
bail to the applicants. Further, it is also submitted that the notice was issued
upon all the applicants under Section 41 A Cr.P.C., but only the applicant No.5
had appeared before the IO in response to the notice issued, and he confessed
before the IO that “it is suspected that impersonate of Shri Iken Tao has been
done by someone in registering the documents in Aalo, without their presence”.
Accordingly, the learned Additional A.G.-cum-Public Prosecutor submits that
the custodial interrogation is very much essential in the present case for just
and proper investigation.
8. Mr. L. Perme, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the informant submits
that the informant has filed written objections against the Anticipatory Bail
application. He also submits that the applicants had registered the forged
partnership deed by incorporating the line “or for 30 years from date of
commencement of agreement” in clause 2.1, which was registered before the
Executive Magistrate by impersonating the informant before the Sub-Registrar,
Aalo, Arunachal Pradesh and further, the applicant No.5 had identified the
person who appeared as Shri Iken Tao, despite of the fact that the applicant
No.5 is the schoolmate of the informant and he personally knows the
informant. Further, instead of registering the deed in Lower Siang District, the
applicants intentionally registered the documents in West Siang District only
with a purpose to forge the documents. More so, they obtained interim relief
order dated 25.03.2021 in Misc.(Arb) Case No.16/2022, producing the forged
deed of agreement and obtained the order by misrepresenting the fact of the
case.
9. After hearing the submission made by both the learned Advocates, I have
perused the case Diary as well as the written objections filed by the informant
of this case and accordingly, I find that there is sufficient materials collected by
Page No.# 6/8
the IO during investigation of this case. The informant side also furnished one
copy of agreement were the line “or for 30 years from date of commencement
of agreement” is missing in clause 2.1, which is alleged to have incorporated in
the registered deed of partnership, executed by impersonating the informant.
Further, it is seen that one interim relief order was also obtained by the
applicant No.1 under Section 9 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in
Misc.(Arb.) Case No.16/2022, dated 25.03.2022, passed by the learned
Additional District Judge, No.2, Kamrup(M), Guwahati and as per the informant
the order has been obtained misrepresenting the fact and also producing the
forged deed of partnership.
10. More so, the Case Dairy reveals that under Section 41 A Cr.P.C. notices were
issued upon all the applicants, but only the applicant No.5 had appeared before
the IO to cooperate with the investigation of the present case and other
applicants did not appear before the IO.
11. So considering the conduct of the applicants of this case as well as materials
available on Case Diary and also considering the nature and gravity of offence,
I find that custodial interrogation of the present applicants is necessary for the
interest of proper investigation and hence, the present petition for Anticipatory
Bail is hereby rejected.
12. In terms of above, the Anticipatory Bail stands disposed of.
6. After rejection of the aforesaid anticipatory bail application filed by the
applicant and others, the instant pre-arrest bail application under Section
438 of the Cr.P.C. was filed by the present applicant on 21.12.2022, which
came up for consideration on 22.12.2022, on which date, Case diary was
called for, fixing 05.01.2023 as the next date of listing.
When the anticipatory bail application was listed on 05.01.2023, before
the learned Judge, who had rejected the earlier anticipatory bail, being, AB
No. 3015/2022, the learned Judge had passed an order to list it on
17.01.2023, before another Bench. When the matter was listed on
17.01.2023, this Court while granting the applicant, the privilege of interim
pre-arrest bail, had observed that statement of the applicant is required to
be gone through first before arriving at a final decision.
Page No.# 7/8
7. It is a settled proposition of law that once the anticipatory bail application
has been rejected on merit, the subsequent anticipatory bail application can
only be entertained if there is change of circumstances to take a different
view other than the view taken in the previous bail application.
8. To indicate that after the earlier anticipatory bail application was rejected
on 13.12.2022, there have been a change of circumstances, the learned
counsel for the applicant has referred to paragraph-4 of the present
anticipatory bail application, which is quoted hereinbelow:
4. That pursuant to the registration of the said FIR dated 14.09.2022 that a
joint bail application under section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
being case No. AB/3015/2022 was filed and moved before the Principal Bench of
Gauhati High Court at Guwahati which was listed on 13.12.2022. However,
after hearing the learned counsel for the parties at some length the Hon’ble
High Court at Principal Bench was please to dispose of the said bail application
without extending the privilege of anticipatory bail to all the applicants. Be that
as it may, the involvement of the applicant in commission of any offence as
alleged in the said FIR dated 14.09.2022 was not properly incorporated
consequently the rejection of the interim bail. Hence, this subsequent bail
application is being filed independently of facts and on law as alleged in the FIR
dated 14.09.2022 for that the applicant even remote as no role.
9. On perusal of paragraph-4 of the present anticipatory bail application, it
is noticed that the applicant has stated that involvement of the applicant in
commission of any offence alleged in the F.I.R., dated 14.09.2022, was not
properly incorporated in the earlier anticipatory bail application because of
which, the earlier anticipatory bail application was rejected by this Court.
10. On perusal of the order dated 13.12.2022, passed in earlier
anticipatory bail application, being, AB No. 3015/2022, it transpires that the
said anticipatory bail application was disposed of after perusal of the Case
Diary produced and by making an elaborate discussion on the merit of the
anticipatory bail application.
Page No.# 8/8
11. In that view of the matter, the contention of the applicant in the
present application that the involvement of the present applicant in
commission of any offence alleged in the F.I.R., dated 14.09.2022, was not
properly incorporated resulting in the rejection of the earlier anticipatory bail
filed being, AB No. 3015/2022, vide order dated 13.12.2022, can hardly be
stated to be any change in circumstance after the order dated 13.12.2022,
was passed in the earlier AB No. 3015/2022. It is a settled position of law
that subsequent bail application can only be entertained if there is a change
in the circumstances that existed when the earlier anticipatory bail
application was considered to enable the Court to take a view other than the
view taken in the earlier anticipatory bail application.
12. Since, there appears to be no change in circumstances after the earlier
anticipatory bail, being, AB No. 3015/2022 was rejected by this Court, I am
of the view that the applicant is not entitled to be granted the privilege of
pre-arrest bail in connection with Aalo P.S. Case No. 49/2022, registered
under Sections 468/471/34 IPC, 1860, when the earlier anticipatory bail
application filed by the applicant, being, AB No. 3015/2022, have been
rejected by this Court, vide order dated 13.12.2022, on an elaborate
discussion on merit.
13. In view of the above, this anticipatory bail application is dismissed
being devoid of merit.
14. Interim pre-arrest bail granted vide order dated 17.01.2023,
accordingly, is hereby recalled.
JUDGE
Comparing Assistant

judgments.case_name: AB/24/2023 of Pinak Pani Roy Vs THE STATE OF AP
judgments.text:
Page No.# 1/4
GAHC040006112023
THE GAUHATI HIGH COURT
(HIGH COURT OF ASSAM, NAGALAND, MIZORAM AND ARUNACHAL PRADESH)
(ITANAGAR BENCH)
Case No. : AB 24/2023
1:Pinak Pani Roy
S/o Lt. Panna Kanti Roy,

781029, Kamrup (M), Assam.
VERSUS
1:THE STATE OF AP
Represented by PP, AP.
Advocate for the Petitioner : Sunil Mow
Advocate for the Respondent : P P of AP
BEFORE

Page No.# 2/7

BEFORE
HONBLE MR. JUSTICE ARUN DEV CHOUDHURY
ORDER
Date : 08-02-2023
Heard Mr. L. Perme, learned counsel for the petitioners. Also heard Mr. G.
Tado, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State of Arunachal Pradesh.
2. This is an application filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973 praying for quashing and setting aside of Charge sheet No.
59/2022 dated 10.05.2022 under Section 453 of IPC, 1860 corresponding to
Naharlagun P.S. Case No. 47/2022 under Section 455 of IPC and its
corresponding proceeding initiated as GR No. 360/2022 under Section 453 of
IPC pending before the learned Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Capital
Complex at Yupia, Arunachal Pradesh.
3. This present petition is filed by the accused in the aforesaid charge-sheet
and he is the petitioner No. 2 along with his wife as petitioner No. 1, in the
present application. This petition is also joined by the petitioner No. 3 who is the
complainant of the alleged offence and she lodged the F.I.R. Further, this
present petition is filed in a background that the complainant and the accused
had settled the matter amicably between them and therefore, this court in
exercise of power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. should quash the criminal
prosecution as the offences charged are not compoundable under Section 320
of Cr.P.C.
4. The contents of the F.I.R. discloses that on the alleged day i.e. 09.05.2022
Page No.# 3/7
the petitioner No. 2 at around 4:00 AM to 4:30 AM out of a sudden went out of
the house without informing his family members after knowing the act in the
wee hours when the family members realized that the petitioner No. 2 is not in
the house they started to search him in the nearby area and found him after
sometime and later on came to know that a FIR/Complaint has been filed by
petitioner No. 3 alleging inter-alia that one unknown intruder broke into her
building at around 4:30 AM and looked every corner of the building with a dao
(Machaete) in his hand. In the aforesaid backdrop, the petitioner No. 3, lodged
an FIR on 09.05.2022 before the Officer-In-Charge Naharlagun Police Station
which was registered as Naharlagun PS Case No. 47/2022 under Section 455 of
IPC.
5. After the registration of the FIR, the case was investigated by the
Investigating Officer and Charge Sheet was laid against the petitioner Nos. 2,
vide Charge Sheet No. 59/2022 dated 10.05.2022 corresponding to GR No.
360/2022 under Section 453 of IPC.
6. Subsequently, the petitioners have mutually settled the matter and entered
into a Deed of Amicable Settlement on 02.12.2022, at Itanagar, Arunachal
Pradesh, which is part of the present petition. In the Deed of Amicable
st
Settlement, the present accused is described as 1 Party, the complainant is
rd
described as 2nd Party and wife of accused is described as 3 Party. The said
Settlement discloses the following:-
“Whereas presently First Party is totally bedridden due to stroke and not in position
to move out from house and as such the Third Party being natural wife of the First
Party is necessary party in this mutual settlement deed.
Whereas, after knowing the identity of the First Party and also having knowledge
about the fact that First Party is totally bedridden, the Second Party agreed to settle
Page No.# 4/7
the case mutually under the supervision of many elders, prominent public figure and
other persons from both the parties”
7. On the basis of the disclosure, the following terms were incorporated in
the settlement amongst other terms.
“1. The Second Party has no more grudge and grievance against the First Party.
2. That Second Party firmly believed that the incident reported by her in FIR dated
09.05.2022 happened without any ill intention on the part of the First Party.
3. That as the First Party is bedridden, the Second Party and Third Party will do
every endeavour and every needful to make sure that the GR No. 360/2022 U/s 453
IPC pending trial before Chief Judicial Magistrate, Capital Complex, Yupia got set
aside and quashed.
4. That all the parties mutual settled the aforesaid mention case for betterment and
continuity old age tribal belief that pardon each other’s is best policy for peaceful
coexistence in society”.
08. In the aforesaid backdrop, this Court is now to decide whether this is a fit
case where this Court can exercise its inherent power under Section 482 of
Cr.P.C. to quash of Charge sheet No. 59/2022 dated 10.05.2022 under Section
453 of IPC, 1860 corresponding to Naharlagun P.S. Case No. 47/2022 under
Section 455 of IPC and its corresponding proceeding initiated as GR No.
360/2022 under Section 453 of IPC pending before the learned Court of Chief
Judicial Magistrate, Capital Complex at Yupia, Arunachal Pradesh.
09. It is by now settled that a High Court in exercise of its power under
Section 482 of Cr.P.C. can very well quash a criminal proceeding or a criminal
complaint under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., but while doing so, the Court is to follow
certain principles as enunciated by the Hon’ble Apex Court in Gian Singh –Vs-
State of Punjab and Another reported in 2012 10 SCC 303, and in State
Page No.# 5/7
of Madhya Pradesh –Vs- Laxmi Narayan and Others reported in 2019 5
SCC 688.
10. In the case of State of Madhya Pradesh & Laxmi Narayan, (supra),
the Hon’ble Supreme Court has laid down certain guidelines for exercise of
powers under Section 482 Cr.P.C., it is submitted that instant case falls within
the guidelines laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court.
11. For ready reference, paragraph-13 of Laxmi Narayan (Supra) is
extracted herein below:
“13. Considering the law on the point and the other decisions of this Court on the point, referred
to hereinabove, it is observed and held as under:
i) that the power conferred under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal
proceedings for the non-compoundable offences under Section 320 of the Code can be
exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character, particularly those
arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial relationship or family
disputes and when the parties have resolved the entire dispute amongst themselves;
ii) ii) such power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involved heinous and
serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity, etc. Such
offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society;
iii) iii) similarly, such power is not to be exercised for the offences under the special
statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants
while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of compromise
between the victim and the offender;
iv) iv) offences under Section 307 IPC and the Arms Act etc. would fall in the category of
heinous and serious offences and therefore are to be treated as crime against the society
and not against the individual alone, and therefore, the criminal proceedings for the
offence under Section 307 IPC and/or the Arms Act etc. which have a serious impact on
the society cannot be quashed in exercise of powers under Section 482 of the Code, on
the ground that the parties have resolved their entire dispute amongst themselves.
However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely because there is a mention of
Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under this provision. It would be open
to the High Court to examine as to whether incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for
the sake of it or the prosecution has collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would
lead to framing the charge under Section 307 IPC.
For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the nature of injury
sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of the body, nature
of weapons used etc. However, such an exercise by the High Court would be permissible
only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the charge sheet is filed/charge
is framed and/or during the trial. Such exercise is not permissible when the matter is still
under investigation. Therefore, the ultimate conclusion in paragraphs 29.6 and 29.7 of the
Page No.# 6/7
decision of this Court in the case of Narinder Singh (supra) should be read harmoniously
and to be read as a whole and in the circumstances stated hereinabove;
v) while exercising the power under Section 482 of the Code to quash the criminal
proceedings in respect of non-compoundable offences, which are private in nature and do
not have a serious impart on society, on the ground that there is a
settlement/compromise between the victim and the offender, the High Court is required to
consider the antecedents of the accused; the conduct of the accused, namely, whether
the accused was absconding and why he was absconding, how he had managed with the
complainant to enter into a compromise etc.”
12. Considering the factual background of the present case and also
considering the nature of offence and declaration by the parties that the
petitioner No. 2 has also been suffering from psychiatric disorder and has been
completely bedridden from past many months, as well as considering the fact
that the compromise was proposed immediately between the parties and taking
note of the materials available on record including the statements recorded
under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., and the Charge-Sheet, this Court is of the
considered opinion that this is a fit case, where this Court should exercise its
inherent power under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. to Charge sheet No. 59/2022 dated
10.05.2022 under Section 453 of IPC, 1860 corresponding to Naharlagun P.S.
Case No. 47/2022 under Section 455 of IPC and its corresponding proceeding
initiated as GR No. 360/2022 under Section 453 of IPC pending before the
learned Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Capital Complex at Yupia, Arunachal
Pradesh. This Court has, coming into such conclusion also considered that the
offence alleged to have been committed is not heinous and shall not have
serious impact on the society.
13. Accordingly, this petition is allowed by setting aside and quashing the
Charge sheet No. 59/2022 dated 10.05.2022 under Section 453 of IPC, 1860
corresponding to Naharlagun P.S. Case No. 47/2022 under Section 455 of IPC
and its corresponding proceeding initiated as GR No. 360/2022 under Section
453 of IPC pending before the learned Court of Chief Judicial Magistrate, Capital
Page No.# 7/7
Complex at Yupia, Arunachal Pradesh.
JUDGE
Comparing Assistant

This is an application under Section 389 Cr.P.C. praying for
bail/suspension of sentence of the accused person/appellant vide
impugned, dated 20.12.2022 and order, dated 21.12.2022 passed in case
No.BSR/SESS-11/2018 by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge, Western
Sessions Division, Basar, Leparada District, Arunachal Pradesh, whereby,
the applicant/appellant was sentenced to undergo imprisonment for 2
years with fine of Rs.5,000/- each for offence under Sections 460/326 IPC
and also to undergo imprisonment for 3 months for the offence under
Sections 323/427 IPC.
It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner that there is
every chances of succeeding in the connected appeal. Initially, the charge
was framed against the applicant/applicant under Sections 451 /325 /
326 /307 /352 /427 /506 /34 IPC but subsequently, he was convicted
under Section 460/326/427 IPC without altering the charge.
It is further submitted that as the applicant/appellant was acquitted
or discharge from Section 451 IPC, he cannot be convicted under Section
460 IPC unless the charge is being framed. At the same time, the
applicant/appellant was also initially charged under Section 325 IPC but he
was subsequently convicted under Section 326 IPC, which is a higher
offence in comparison to Section 325 IPC.
Further, it is submitted that the evidence of the victim as well as the
Page No.# 3/4
informant also reveals that they could not identify the persons who
assaulted the victim. Further, it is submitted by the learned counsel for the
applicant/appellant that the charge can be altered or modified at the time
of passing judgment complying the provision of Section 222 Cr.P.C. in case
if the person is punished in smaller section in which section he was
charged earlier but in the instant case, the applicant/appellant was
convicted under Sections 460/326/427 IPC and without giving any chance
of hearing in the said offences and/ or without altering the charge.
In this regard, the learned counsel for the applicant/appellant has
relied on a decision of the Hon’ble Apex Court in the case of Sangaraboina
Sreenu-vs-State of A.P; reported in (1997) 5 SCC 348, wherein, the
Hon’ble Apex Court expressed the view that the provision of Section 222
Cr.P.C. cannot be applied where the section charged is convicted are of
distinct and different categories. Further, it is submitted by the learned
counsel for the applicant/appellant that during the entire trial, the
applicant/appellant was on bail and he was also granted with pre-arrest
bail after his order of conviction, however, he could not appear on the
date fixed by the learned Addl. Sessions Judge due to communication gap
with his engaged counsel and further prayed that he is ready to abide by
any condition as deem fit by this Court, if he is enlarge on bail.
Mr. T. Ete, learned Addl. PP submitted that the prayer for suspension
of sentence in a petition filed under Section 389 Cr.P.C., the main criteria is
to be decided as to whether there is a chance of succeeding in the appeal.
Here, in this case, on perusal of the evidence as well as the other
Page No.# 4/4
witnesses, it is seen that none of the victim and the witnesses could
identify the applicant/appellant or the persons who assaulted the victim at
the time of the incident, therefore, there may be chances of succeeding in
this appeal and accordingly, Mr. Ete did not raise any objection in the
event of allowing the applicant/appellant to go on fresh bail.
In view of the discussions made hereinabove, I am of the considered
opinion that this is a fit case where the applicant/appellant can be allowed
to go on fresh bail. Accordingly, the applicant/appellant, namely, Shri Yili
Gadi is allowed to go on fresh bail on furnishing a bail bond of
Rs.20,000/- to the satisfaction of the learned Addl. District and Sessions
Judge, Basar, Western Zone, Leparada District, Arunachal Pradesh till
disposal of the connected appeal and the judgment, dated 20.12.2022 and
the conviction order, dated 21.12.2022 is hereby suspended till disposal of
the connected appeal.
In view of the above, this Interlocutory Application stands disposed
of.

investigation, the police had submitted the charge sheet being charge sheet no.

petitioner no. 1, no prosecution witness has been examined till date.

2014(6) SCC 466 learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that the Hon’ble
Supreme Court has held that when the parties have reached the settlement and
when the possibility of conviction is remote and bleak and continuantion of
criminal case would be futile, then the High Court should exercise its inherent
power under Section 482 of Cr.PC, 1973 and quash the criminal proceeding in
order to secure the ends of justice and to prevent the abuse of the process of
the Court. Therefore, he submits that the criminal proceeding being GR Case no.
619/2016 pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Yupia may be
quashed.
7. Ms. T. Jini, learned Additional PP fairly submits that in the facts and
Page No.# 4/6
circumstances of the present case, the continuance of the proceeding would be
futile and to prevent such futile proceeding, this Court may pass an appropriate
order in the interest of justice.

for the parties and also scrutinized the materials available on record.
9. The principle of law regarding the quashing of criminal proceedings by
exercising power under section 482 of Cr.PC, 1973 has been enunciated by the
Hon’ble Supreme Court in the case of the State of Madhya Pradesh Vs.
Lakshmi Narayan and Ors., reported in (2019) 5 SCC 688 which is
reproduced herein below:
“15. Considering the law on the point and the other decisions of this Court on the
point, referred to hereinabove, it is observed and held as under:
15.1) that the power conferred under Section 482 of the Code to quash the
criminal proceedings for the non-compoundable offences under Section 320 of the
Code can be exercised having overwhelmingly and predominantly the civil character,
particularly those arising out of commercial transactions or arising out of matrimonial
relationship or family disputes and when the parties have resolved the entire dispute
amongst themselves;
15.2) such power is not to be exercised in those prosecutions which involved
heinous and serious offences of mental depravity or offences like murder, rape, dacoity,
etc. Such offences are not private in nature and have a serious impact on society;
15.3) similarly, such power is not to be exercised for the offences under the special
statutes like Prevention of Corruption Act or the offences committed by public servants
while working in that capacity are not to be quashed merely on the basis of
compromise between the victim and the offender;
15.4) offences under Section 307 IPC and the Arms Act etc. would fall in the
category of heinous and serious offences and therefore are to be treated as crime
against the society and not against the individual alone, and therefore, the criminal
proceedings for the offence under Section 307 IPC and/or the Arms Act etc. which have
a serious impact on the society cannot be quashed in exercise of powers under Section
482 of the Code, on the ground that the parties have resolved their entire dispute
amongst themselves. However, the High Court would not rest its decision merely
because there is a mention of Section 307 IPC in the FIR or the charge is framed under
this provision. It would be open to the High Court to examine as to whether
Page No.# 5/6
incorporation of Section 307 IPC is there for the sake of it or the prosecution has
collected sufficient evidence, which if proved, would lead to framing the charge under
Section 307 IPC. For this purpose, it would be open to the High Court to go by the
nature of injury sustained, whether such injury is inflicted on the vital/delegate parts of
the body, nature of weapons used etc. However, such an exercise by the High Court
would be permissible only after the evidence is collected after investigation and the
charge sheet is filed/charge is framed and/or during the trial. Such exercise is not
permissible when the matter is still under investigation. Therefore, the ultimate
conclusion in paragraphs 29.6 and 29.7 of the decision of this Court in the case of
Narinder Singh (supra) should be read harmoniously and to be read as a whole and in
the circumstances stated hereinabove;
15.5) while exercising the power under Section 482 of the Code to quash the
criminal proceedings in respect of non-compoundable offences, which are private in
nature and do not have a serious impart on society, on the ground that there is a
settlement/compromise between the victim and the offender, the High Court is required
to consider the antecedents of the accused; the conduct of the accused, namely,
whether the accused was absconding and why he was absconding, how he had
managed with the complainant to enter into a compromise etc. “
10. In the case of Kapil Gupta V. State of NCT of Delhi, (2022) SCC
Online SC 1030, the Hon’ble Supreme Court held that the Court while exercising
its power under section 482 Cr.PC, the Court should be slow in quashing the
proceedings wherein heinous and serious offences are involved, but is not
foreclosed from examining as to whether there exists material for incorporation
of such an offence or as to whether there is sufficient evidence which if proved
would lead to proving the charge for the offence charged with. The Court has
also to take into consideration as to whether the settlement between the parties
is going to result into harmony between them which may improve their mutual
relationship.
11. On the scrutiny of the materials available on record and having
considered the submission of the learned counsel for the parties, I find that the
petitioner No. 1 was charge-sheeted under sections 307/326/201 of IPC, 1860
and the matter was committed to the Sessions Judge. The Sessions Court
Page No.# 6/6
framed the charge against the accused/petitioner No. 1 under Section 326 of
IPC, 1860 and after framing of the charge it was transferred to the Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Yupia.
12. The petitioners have entered into a settlement by mutual agreement
on 23.05.2023 as the incident happened out of misunderstanding of facts and
they have decided to maintain cordial relationship with each other and had
buried all the differences. The settlement is without any coercion or threat from
any angle rather it appears to be on their own volition. In the facts and
circumstances of the present case, this Court is of the view that the chances of
conviction is remote and bleak and continuance of the criminal proceeding will
be futile and tantamount to abuse of the process of the Court.
13. In view of the discussion made herein above, and the law laid down
by the Hon’ble Apex Court, this Court is of the opinion that it is a fit case for
exercising the power under section 482 Cr.PC., 1973 for quashing the aforesaid
criminal proceeding pending before the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Yupia.
14. Accordingly, the criminal proceeding of GR case no. 619/2016 under
sections 326 of IPC, 1860 corresponding to Itanagar PS case no. 246/2016
pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Yupia is hereby set aside and
quashed.
15. In the result, the criminal petition is allowed and disposed of.
JUDGE
Comparing Assistant
